meta.name: Portfolio Snapshot + One Pager data dictionary (verified content)
meta.verification: Every formula and source verified against live code (one_pager.py, metrics.py, portfolio_snapshot_*.py, config.py) on 2026-09-24.
meta.audience: analysts — internal table/column/account names are fine to show
meta.granularity: one entry per (tab, field); each entry decomposes into `inputs`, each with its own source.
meta.formula_rule: Render `formula_latex` when present (formula_is_arithmetic=true). When null, the field has NO clean single-expression arithmetic — state the method in words and DO NOT reconstruct an equation. Never invent a formula or a source.

answer_format.latex: block math on ONE line as $$...$$ ; inline as \( ... \) ; never ** inside a formula

meta.mri_table_note: Sources name the MRI feed/table an analyst can open directly (e.g. Prop_Info_Core = deal roster; ISBS_Download = interim/projected/budget statements; accounting_feed = investor cash flows; MRI_Loans, MRI_Occupancy_Download, Prop_Info_AtClose, MRI_Budget_Econ_Occ, Prop_Info_DealTerms, MRI_VAL, MRI_Event_Dates, MRI_Inspection) plus the column/account.
meta.supplement_caveat: Five ISBS supplement tables (isbs_uw_supplements, isbs_budget_is_supplements, isbs_interim_is_supplements, isbs_interim_bs_supplements, isbs_valuation_is_supplements) are analyst-loaded CSV uploads, NOT MRI-refreshed. They merge into the ISBS data and WIN over MRI on collision — so an ISBS-sourced value can actually come from an analyst CSV. Valuations (MRI_VAL) and waterfalls are app-owned / PROTECTED, not MRI feeds.

inputs.note: Occupancy comes from the MRI_Occupancy_Download 'Occ%' (or 'OccupancyPercent') column. This figure comes from ISBS (MRI), but if an analyst has uploaded a supplement CSV for this deal and period, the uploaded value is used instead.

The budget itself usually comes from the isbs_budget_is_supplements CSV, which is the official source for a budget between the time it is imported and the time MRI approves it (normally the case).
In Q4, or when there is no budget, this equals the year-to-date actual. The rest-of-year portion carries no bad-debt adjustment; only the year-to-date portion does.

The One Pager uses its own account list, which differs from the shared config list: it leaves out 4075 (Other Income) and 5092 (Repairs & Maintenance), keeps 7070 out of Real Estate Taxes (handled separately), and sets Principal to account 7060 where the shared list leaves it empty. Any reference to 'IS_ACCOUNTS' here means the One Pager's own list.

fields.definition: Debt service coverage. Columns: ytd_actual · ytd_budget · variance · at_close · actual_ye · uw_ye.
fields.formula: dscr = NOI ÷ debt service

inputs.source: Calc — ytd NOI ÷ (|SUM of 5190 at ytd_date| + BS principal change 2150/2152/2210), gated > 0
inputs.note: The principal-paid figure is never allowed to go negative. For months where a loan was paid off (MRI_Loans vDateType = 'Paid Off'), the code substitutes the nearest earlier normal month's principal change, or the deal's median paydown.

inputs.source: Calc — NOI ÷ |SUM(5190 + 7060) over (prior Dec 31, quarter-end] from Budget IS|
inputs.note: Debt service on the One Pager is accounts 5190 plus 7060. This figure comes from ISBS (MRI), but if an analyst has uploaded a supplement CSV for this deal and period, the uploaded value is used instead.

inputs.source: Calc — (ytd NOI + rem NOI) ÷ (|ytd DS| + |rem DS|)
inputs.note: This uses a mixed basis: the year-to-date portion is account 5190 plus the change in the balance-sheet loan balance, while the rest-of-year portion is budgeted account 5190 plus 7060.

Underwritten debt service is account 7010. If that account's running total stops growing before month 12, the figure is annualised by multiplying by 12 ÷ months active (this fixed Ascent, which had been showing 10.69x).

inputs.source: Calc — −at_close_noi ÷ (|at_close_interest| + |at_close_principal|) from at_close_noi table; fallback calc_amounts(Projected IS, earliest Dec-31)
inputs.note: Comes from the Prop_Info_AtClose columns at_close_revenue / _expenses / _noi, with revenue and NOI sign-flipped when read. This figure comes from ISBS (MRI), but if an analyst has uploaded a supplement CSV for this deal and period, the uploaded value is used instead.

fields.formula: committed_pe = SUM of | Amt | where is_commitment & non-OP & EffectiveDate <= quarter-end

inputs.source: MRI — accounting_feed.Amt/.MajorType/.Typename; is_commitment = MajorType~'contrib' AND Typename~'commitment'
inputs.note: If this comes out as zero, it falls back to the sum of preferred-equity contributions from partner_results.

fields.formula: funded_to_date = SUM of (−Amt) over non-OP, non-commitment rows where MajorType~'contrib'
fields.formula_latex: \text{Funded to Date} = \text{SUM}(-\text{Amt}\ \text{for contrib, non-OP, non-commitment rows})

inputs.note: Uses signed amounts, not absolute values, so a positive contribution row actually reduces this total.

fields.definition: Capital returned to the PE investor.
fields.formula: return_of_capital = SUM of Amt over non-OP rows where MajorType~'distri' AND TypeName~'return of capital' OR 'realized gain'
fields.formula_latex: \text{Return of Capital} = \text{SUM}(\text{Amt for non-OP ROC / realized-gain rows})

inputs.note: Realized-gain rows are counted here, but they are not counted in the capital-stack equity netting. That mismatch is what makes the simple 'funded minus return of capital' subtraction wrong (see current_pe_balance below).

fields.formula: current_pe_balance = SUM of seed_states[non-OP].total_capital_outstanding at min(quarter-end, ACTUALS_THROUGH)

inputs.note: This is not simply funded-to-date minus return of capital — that subtraction is thrown off by realized-gain rows (for East Manchester it gives −$1,539,662 versus the engine's correct 0). The subtraction is only used as a fallback when the full data isn't available.

fields.formula: remaining_to_fund = max(0, committed_pe − funded_to_date)

inputs.note: Set to 0.0 when committed PE is zero and the partner_results contribution fallback is used.

fields.definition: Return on equity to date (annualised, time-weighted — NOT IRR).
fields.formula: roe_to_date = SUM(distributions, inception→quarter-end) ÷ weighted-avg capital ÷ years

inputs.source: MRI — accounting_feed.Amt, non-OP, EffectiveDate <= quarter-end, InvestmentID->vcode
inputs.note: Distributions are netted against the positive (contribution) rows so that only actual returns of capital reduce the capital balance.

inputs.source: Calc — SUMPRODUCT(balance, days) ÷ total_days. This is the time-weighted average capital: each period's capital balance is weighted by how many days it was held, so a balance held for 90 days counts more than one held for 10.

inputs.component: → How each period's balance is built
inputs.source: Calc from the MRI accounting_feed — start with the prior period's balance, add contributions (cash in), and subtract returns of capital (cash out). So each period's balance = prior balance + that period's change.
Calc — the balance can never drop below zero. Once an investor has been fully repaid, their balance stays at 0 instead of going negative.
Calc — total_days ÷ 365; inception = earliest capital-event date
inputs.note: The whole ROE returns 0.0 if there are no contributions or events, if the day count is zero, or if the weighted-average capital is zero or below.

inputs.source: Look-forward window: pref distributions (TypeID 1019 or name ~ 'preferred/pref return'), non-OP, non-commitment, in (quarter-end, +45d] pulled back to quarter-end
inputs.note: Only distributions in the 45-day window are pulled back to quarter-end; contributions and returns of capital in that window are not — this asymmetry is intentional. (This is a different rule from the 45-day preferred-return compounding in waterfall.py, which does not apply here.)

fields.definition: Underwritten ROE to date (same calc on underwritten flows).
fields.formula: uw_roe_to_date = SUM(UW distributions) ÷ UW weighted-avg capital ÷ years

inputs.source: MRI ISBS_Download 'Projected IS', account 7071 — PLUS isbs_uw_supplements (analyst-loaded CSV, NOT MRI-refreshed; the CSV row WINS on collision). Read as abs(periodic) — not sign-preserving.
inputs.note: Read as an absolute value, not sign-preserving (this corrects an earlier note that said otherwise).

inputs.source: MRI ISBS_Download 'Projected IS', account 7073 — PLUS isbs_uw_supplements (analyst-loaded CSV backfill, NOT MRI-refreshed). Sign-preserving: MRI-positive = contribution. This is where the underwritten CONTRIBUTIONS come from.
inputs.note: Duplicates are removed by matching on date and amount, because the same row can arrive from both MRI and the supplement CSV — for example Burton's 6/30/2025 contribution of $26,597,500 shows up in both.

inputs.source: Calc — base ISBS rows are YTD-cumulative: periodic = cumulative − prior-same-year (first entry of year = cumulative)
inputs.note: The base MRI rows are year-to-date running totals and get converted to per-period amounts; supplement CSV rows are already per-period. Account 7073 is de-duplicated by date and rounded amount because Burton's contribution was otherwise double-counted across MRI and the supplement CSV, so this de-duplication genuinely matters.

inputs.source: Only runs when the deal has actual capital_events
inputs.note: If a deal has no actual accounting activity, it gets no underwritten ROE either, even when underwritten figures exist.

fields.formula: accrued_balance = max(0, accrued − | pref paid in the 45-day grace window |)

inputs.source: App — reports_service.deal_accrued_pref via build_pref_balance_detail; fallback SUM of seed_states[non-OP].(pref_unpaid_compounded + add_pref_accrued_current_year)

fields.formula: actual_growth = (noi_projected_ye − noi_at_close) ÷ noi_at_close

fields.definition: Preferred coupon shown in the PE Performance block.

inputs.note: This is the primary source, used whenever the waterfall has a coupon above 0. A 0% coupon is treated as if there were none.

Used only when the waterfall coupon is 0 or missing. It's the only source on the three deals that have deal terms but no waterfall rows: Plaza Del Mar (P0000116), Apple Self Storage (P0000003) and Jefferson Stephens (P0000114).

fields.definition: PE participation shown in the PE Performance block.

inputs.source: App-built waterfalls.FXRate (PROTECTED_TABLES, never MRI-fed) — the reader takes the first vState='Share' row (unfiltered by PropCode), else the operating partner's share.
inputs.note: When the deal-terms participation (pe_split_capital) is a positive number, the waterfall value is used instead.

A deal-terms participation set explicitly to 0 does override the waterfall (the code keeps the waterfall only when the deal-terms value is both present and not zero). This is live on Jefferson Eastchase (P0000085) and Jefferson Addison Heights (P0000077), where an OPJPI participation of 1.0 rendered as 1%.

fields.definition: Provenance label shown as the hover tooltip on the Debt cell — which of the three debt bases fired for this deal.

inputs.source: App-computed provenance string from resolve_debt (ISBS drawn / committed loan / dev hard-costs). Rendered as the Debt-cell tooltip (SnapshotLoan.vue).
inputs.note: This is not an MRI field; it just labels which debt basis the resolver picked.
